summary.headline: Granules pivots to four growth engines; plans ~2,000 crore organic capex over 3-4 years after warrant-funded move to net cash.
summary.overview: Management, at an IIFL-hosted "Granules India 2.0" webinar, framed FY27 onward as a shift from building capabilities to scaling them, after a return to growth in FY26. Four growth engines were named: controlled substances, complex generics/early market entry, oncology, and peptide CDMO (Senn Tides). The CFO said the company is now in a consolidated net cash position following September 2026 preferential warrant proceeds, and plans about 2,000 crore of organic capex over three to four years. Management was candid that gross margin gains (about 15 pp over four years) have not yet fully flowed to EBITDA, and that the peptide business is currently loss-making. No quarterly financial figures for Q2 FY27 were given in the call.

segments.name: US (anchor market)
segments.commentary: About 75% of overall revenue; currently retail-focused across OTC and Rx, with first specialty/institutional launch expected in FY29 and a B2C division in Canada next year.

segments.name: Controlled substances (US Rx)
segments.commentary: Now the third-largest US controlled substance manufacturer by value per IQVIA (eighth in July 2025). Top-three position in six of seven ADHD products marketed; Adderall XR share rose from 5% (2024) to 29%.

segments.name: Complex generics / first-to-file
segments.commentary: Two sole first-to-file ANDAs filed (generic Lumryz and generic Dyanavel, combined US market above $350 million, potential 180-day exclusivity); four to five further first-to-files planned for FY30-34 commercialisation.

segments.name: Oncology
segments.commentary: Shifted from broad conventional oncology generics to selected molecules; two products filed, one extended to about 15 countries; about six more filings planned this year and early next year. Commercialisation begins FY29.

segments.name: Peptide CDMO (Senn Tides India / Senn Chemicals, Switzerland)
segments.commentary: Acquired about 18 months ago; currently EBITDA-negative with target to turn profitable in FY27. Targets about $50 million revenue run-rate in three years and above $100 million in five years. About one-third of about $20 million revenue is development-based.

segments.name: Europe and ROW (API and PFI-led)
segments.commentary: Management plans a meaningful Latin America and other international presence by FY30 using B2B and B2C channels.

qa_highlights.question: Given the warrant-funded balance sheet and capex plan, is an inorganic deal likely in the near term, e.g. in peptides?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Krishna Prasad Chigurupati said the company is always looking at inorganic opportunities but remains disciplined and will not jump at whatever comes up.

qa_highlights.question: How will raw material and API cost pressure and shortages in the legacy business be handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Mukesh Surana said near-term challenges exist and the company is working with customers on pricing mechanisms, with some pass-through possibly lagged; no numbers were given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 2,000 crore capex goes to each bucket, and what milestones would stop peptide spending?
qa_highlights.answer: Mukesh said the plan is broad-based, with a significant portion going to peptide CDMO, complex generics and oncology, but gave no split. Sanjay Kumar said peptide spend depends on innovator clinical outcomes, with fee-for-service income offsetting failures.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the 15 pp gross margin gain not reached EBITDA, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Mukesh said R&D rose from 3% to 6% of revenue and fully integrated manufacturing adds cost; full translation is not yet achieved, and EBITDA margin rose about 3 pp over four years. He declined to give numbers.

qa_highlights.question: How many oncology ANDAs are filed, and what is the filing run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Priyanka Chigurupati said over 95 ANDAs are filed overall at a run-rate of 6-10 a year, aiming for 10-15 US filings a year. Two oncology products are filed, one approved in about 15 countries, with about six more filings this year and early next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fixed-cost share of above-EBITDA expenses, and what are the one-off costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Mukesh said a significant portion is fixed, fairly above 50%, with semi-variable items such as power and fuel. One-offs were about 100 crore last full year, including about 60 crore of USFDA remediation consultancy.

guidance_outlook: Management said it does not give formal guidance; no numeric FY27 revenue or EBITDA guidance was provided.
Peptide CDMO (Senn Tides India) targeted to become profitable in FY27; intermediate target about $50 million annual revenue run-rate in three years and above $100 million in five years.
Oncology commercialisation begins FY29; controlled products pipeline extends through FY35; four to five further first-to-files to commercialise FY30-34.
US specialty/institutional entry with first product in FY29; B2C division in Canada next year; Latin America and other international presence targeted by FY30.
Targets 10-15 US filings per year (up from 6-10 run-rate) and extension of products to Europe and ROW.
Gross margin gains (about 15 pp) only partly translate to EBITDA; majority of above-EBITDA costs described as fixed, with one-off costs (about 100 crore last full year) expected to fall away.
capex_capacity: Plans about 2,000 crore organic capex over next three to four years across complex generics, oncology, peptide CDMO, US operations, manufacturing and R&D infrastructure, plus digitalisation and AI manufacturing and quality systems.
Capex to follow a milestone-based approach tied to development progress, regulatory milestones, customer commitments and commercial opportunities; no split by bucket given.
Peptide CDMO: Hyderabad R&D centre operational; manufacturing expansion starting October 2026 on land allocated to the peptide CDMO entity, covering peptide intermediates and APIs.
Controlled substances: Chantilly facility has room to grow within existing infrastructure; DEA quota rises every year.
Oncology uses existing Vizag manufacturing infrastructure, with additional investment tied to development and regulatory milestones.
ROCE up about 1 pp YoY to 18%, and up about 2 pp Q1 vs Q1; newly invested assets not yet earning expected returns.
demand_pricing: Controlled substances: third-largest US controlled substance manufacturer by value per IQVIA (eighth in July 2025); top three in six of seven ADHD products marketed; Adderall XR share rose from 5% (2024) to 29% as of last month.

Lisdexamfetamine: now number two generic supplier despite entering last. Methylphenidate: 6% of market value addressed, pipeline covers 87%. Dexmethylphenidate: approved for 39% of value, 50% more in pipeline. Amphetamines: approvals cover 74% of value.
Two sole first-to-file ANDAs (generic Lumryz, generic Dyanavel) with combined US market above $350 million and potential 180-day exclusivity; a third filed in oncology.
Peptide CDMO: about $20 million revenue last year, roughly one-third development-based, one-third commercial, one-third via other large CDMOs.
Near-term raw material cost pressure and shortages in developed markets (e.g. ibuprofen) flagged; management says it is working with customers on pricing pass-through, possibly with a lag.
Complex generics rose to 33% of revenue in FY26 from 1% in FY20; roughly 45-50% of finished dosage volume in FY26.
risks_watch: Gagillapur USFDA re-inspection: management said all CAPAs (over 100) are complete and the FDA is expected 'anytime now'; timing not committed.

Controlled substances depend on DEA quota and API allocation; any compliance lapse would hit the segment. Launches of several ADHD products and pending litigation (sodium oxybate and others) lack disclosed timelines.
Peptide CDMO is EBITDA-negative with the FY27 profitability target; revenue is partly lumpy and tied to innovator clinical success.
Competition in oncology and first-to-file opportunities is rising, with many players in the same molecules and fewer sole first-to-files.
Raw material cost pressure and pricing pass-through lag in the legacy business; margin gains not yet translated to EBITDA.
Capex of about 2,000 crore has no bucket split and no return targets; ROCE gains depend on newly invested assets ramping up.
key_quotes: Today, we are moving from building these capabilities to scaling them and converting them into commercial growth.
Over four years, gross margin expanded by about 15 percentage points to 65 percent and EBITDA margin by three percentage points to 22 percent.

We are targeting approximately 50 million US dollar in annual revenue run rate in three years from now as an intermediate milestone to get to and cross the threshold of 100 million revenue size in five years.
We plan to invest about 2,000 crore in organic capital expenditure over the next three to four years.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on controlled substances, first-to-file and the growth-engine narrative, but notably non-committal on numbers: no formal guidance, no capex split, no ROCE target and no launch timelines where litigation applies. Candid that margin gains have not fully reached EBITDA and that peptides are loss-making.

adds.what: Peptide CDMO manufacturing expansion (peptide intermediates and APIs) at Senn Tides India, land allocated; Hyderabad R&D centre already operational
Organic capex programme of about 2,000 crore over 3-4 years across complex generics, oncology, peptide CDMO, US operations, manufacturing, R&D and digitalisatio

growth.why: No numeric FY27 revenue or EBITDA guidance; growth rests on a ~2,000 crore organic capex plan over 3-4 years, a peptide CDMO target of about $50M run-rate in three years (from about $20M last year), 10-15 US filings per year, and first-to-file launches, with backing partly specific (Senn manufacturing expansion from October 2026) and partly aspirational.
